The Caucasus extends from the land of the Armenians as far as the Colchians. Lake Serbonis is situated around Pelusium in Egypt.

1219-21a. μηδ’ οὕτως ἠθεῖε: In response to the statement 'therefore I am exceedingly afraid to sail' (v. 1203), Peleus answered, urging him not to be afraid. Therefore it should be written with θυμῷ. It is also written with μύθῳ, so that it would be: do not frighten us with your account of Aeetes. [But it is not transmitted thus, but in all manuscripts δειδίσσεο θυμῷ.] For in no respect, he says, are we inferior to Aeetes. The form ἠθεῖε, I think, has come about by insertion of the η, just as βαιός becomes ἠβαιός and μύω becomes ἠμύω. In its ordinary sense it means θεῖε, 'uncle', 'kinsman', or θαυμάσιε — 'by no means, my good sir' — or καλέ, 'good sir'.

1231-41a. Φιλυρ〈η〉ίδα νῆ〈σον〉: He means the island of the Philyrae. Apollonius speaks of it from Philyra, daughter of Oceanus, who dwelt in these regions. When Cronus had intercourse with her, while he was king of the Titans, Rhea caught them in the act; whereupon Cronus, out of shame, changed himself into a horse, and she fled to Thessaly. Pherecydes (3 fg 50 J.) says that Cronus, having taken the form of a horse, had intercourse with Philyra, daughter of Oceanus, and for this reason Chiron was of double form. But Suidas in the first book of his Thessalica (fg 1 M. II 464) says that Chiron was the son of Ixion and brother of Pirithous.
